pairs.why: Both are the same clean, glossy cup with a blue rim on purple, and the slight differences in size and saucer contrast don't move either one closer to the real cards.
A's softer, warmer shading and richer steam come slightly closer to the real cards' lighting, while B is a bit cooler and plastic-glossy.
B's darker tea with small surface bubbles and crisper rim highlights adds the small, smooth detail the real cards have (like the condensation and ice), while A is the plainer baseline.
A has more saturated tea, a bubbled surface and fuller steam, which matches the real cards' vivid, lightly detailed finish better than B's plainer, ultra-smooth cup.
The two cups are almost identical in shape, gloss, color and lighting, so neither is meaningfully closer to the real cards.
Apart from a slightly different steam shape and cup proportions, A and B render the same way, and neither matches the real cards better.
B's richer amber tea with foam bubbles and stronger rim definition matches the real cards' saturated, lightly detailed look better than A's plainer, smoother baseline.
A's deeper tea color, surface bubbles and denser steam give it the lively, smooth-but-not-sterile finish of the real cards, while B is the plain baseline.
